extracted.intended_audience: broadcasters, petitioners, counsel, and members of the public responding to an FCC television-allotment NPRM
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and technical criteria governing a Federal Communications Commission Notice of Proposed Rulemaking to allot an NCE television channel to Jacksonville, Oregon, including filing procedures, deadlines, ex parte rules, community-qualification evidence, and technical spacing/contour requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments Close / Filing Deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be filed on or before November 3, 2023 and reply comments on or before November 20, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public Comments: "Comments are no longer being accepted. See DATES for details." (document notes deadlines and that comments are subject to the dates listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing Addresses and Service
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should be filed with the Federal Communications Commission, Office of the Secretary, 45 L Street, NE, Washington, DC 20554.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to filing comments with the FCC, interested parties should serve counsel for the Petitioner as follows: Howard M. Liberman, Esq., Wilkinson Barker Knauer, LLP, 1800 M Street, NW, Suite 800N, Washington, DC 20036.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte contacts prohibition during NPRM
rubrics_metrics.description: All ex parte contacts are prohibited from the time a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking is issued to the time the matter is no longer subject to Commission consideration or court review (see 47 CFR 1.1208).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are exceptions to the prohibition; consult Section 1.1204(a) of the Commission's rules for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper filing procedures (47 CFR 1.415 & 1.420)
rubrics_metrics.description: See Sections 1.415 and 1.420 of the Commission's rules for information regarding the proper filing procedures for comments (47 CFR 1.415 and 1.420).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the referenced rule sections for format, filing methods, and procedural requirements when submitting comments and reply comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum geographic spacing requirements (47 CFR 73.623(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel *4 can be allotted to Jacksonville, Oregon, consistent with the minimum geographic spacing requirements for new allotments in section 73.623(d) of the Commission's rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Bureau staff engineering analysis confirms the proposed allotment meets the spacing distances required by section 73.623(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Community encompassment by 35 dBμ contour (47 CFR 73.625(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The allotment point complies with section 73.625(a)(1) of the rules as the entire community of Jacksonville is encompassed by the proposed 35 dBμ contour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates that the proposed allotment provides the requisite coverage of the entire community under the cited rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority for first local service (Priority (2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Petitioner's proposal would result in a first local service to Jacksonville under Priority (2) of the Commission's television allotment priority standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allotments providing a community's first local service are evaluated under the Commission's priority scheme; this proposal asserts Priority (2) status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria/evidence for qualifying as a community for allotment purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence offered that Jacksonville qualifies as a community: incorporated in 1860; had a population of 3,020 as of the 2020 Census; has a mayor and six council members; police, fire, public works, planning, and other government departments; an elementary school; a historic district; and a chamber of commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such factual attributes are presented to demonstrate community status for allotment purposes and are the type of evidence the Commission considers in qualifying an entity as a community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner's intent to apply and obtain construction permit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Petitioner states its intention to file an application for channel *4, if allotted, and take all necessary steps to obtain a construction permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stating intent to apply and to pursue a construction permit supports the petition and indicates readiness to implement the allotment if granted.

rubrics_metrics.description: To request materials in accessible formats (Braille, large print, computer diskettes, or audio recordings), contact FCC504@fcc.gov or call the Consumer & Government Affairs Bureau at (202) 418-0530 (VOICE), (202) 418-0432 (TTY).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act and Regulatory Flexibility Act applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: This document does not contain information collection requirements subject to the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995. Provisions of the Regulatory Flexibility Act of 1980 do not apply to this proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that the NPRM does not propose information collections triggering PRA review and that RFA requirements are not implicated for this action.
